links.about: Reusing Commons files: licenses, credit, hotlinking
What a credit line must hold

notes: Reusing page: hotlinking "is also possible, but is not recommended." So images are downloaded.

Each file has its own license; the author, not the uploader, must be credited; "If the license requires you to link to or provide a copy of the license, do this." So the credit names title, author and license with links.
CommonsMetadata: LicenseShortName is the "short human-readable license name" and more reliable than License; Artist "might contain complex HTML", so tags are stripped.
CommonsMetadata: Restrictions lists "reuse restrictions such as trademarks or personality rights", and NonFree true means "not under a free license". Either one fails the license check.
User-Agent policy: requests need a descriptive User-Agent with contact information, or they fail with 403. Draftsman sends its name, version and repository URL.
API etiquette asks clients to cache data; searches are cached for an hour.
No endpoint is documented to call when a file is used, so there is no on-pick URL.
GFDL-only files fail: the license wants a full copy of its text alongside the image.
